messages.subject: Profiles as Predictors
messages.body_plain:
Good Afternoon,

I have been transitioning from MPlus to R when estimating latent profiles. I have been searching for syntax in R to see if my profiles predict workplace outcomes as auxiliary variables, but I am having trouble finding such resources. Is TidyLPA able to do this?

Thank you for your time!

Rebecca Harmata

Master's Student in Psychology

San Diego State University

rharma...@sdsu.edu

messages.subject: Re: Profiles as Predictors
messages.body_plain:
Hey Rebecca,

Unfortunately it is not possible to use TidyLPA to use profiles as predictors of outcomes; however, Mplus is able to do this.  Below is a couple citations for recent articles detailing the various ways to predict outcomes using profiles as predictors in Mplus.

Asparouhov, T., & Muthén, B. O. (2013). Auxiliary variables in mixture modeling: A 3-step approach using Mplus (Mplus web notes: No. 15). Mplus Web Notes: No. 15, (15), 1–48. https://doi.org/http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2014.915181

Nylund-Gibson, K., Grimm, R. P., & Masyn, K. E. (2019). Prediction from Latent Classes: A Demonstration of Different Approaches to Include Distal Outcomes in Mixture Models. Structural Equation Modeling, 1–19. https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2019.1590146

messages.body_plain:
are sysmis (missing values) all specified correctly as N/A in data frame and are headers used in data frame?

Would check those potential trigger points as first step.

Best regards,
J.D.

messages.subject: error in 'bootLRTS'
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I’m using tidyLPA for the first time on a fairly small dataset (~3600x4), but have been unsuccessful in getting it to run.  Two of the variables in the model are binary; the other two are continuos with values ranging from 0-10.

I used the following code:

datin %>%

+     select(v1,v2,v3,v4) %>%

+     estimate_profiles(2:3)

But get this error:

Error in bootLRTS[, 1:g, drop = FALSE] : subscript out of bounds

I am able to successfully use tidyLPA on a test dataset (subset of pisaUSA15).

Does anyone have any clues about what is causing this error?  Is it something in the structure of the data?

Thanks for your help.

M. Pettinger
